name: Small Magellanic Cloud, quasar field SZ23 (Hubble)
blurb: Small Magellanic Cloud field SZ23, a star field in a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way, seen by Hubble.
label: smcquasarfieldsz23-hubble
story: Stars of the Small Magellanic Cloud fill this view, chosen because a far more distant quasar shines from behind them. Using such quasars as fixed markers, astronomers measured how the galaxy's stars move and found signs that it is being pulled apart by tides.

claims.text: The Small Magellanic Cloud is a dwarf galaxy and a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way
SMC is the abbreviation for the Small Magellanic Cloud
Field SZ23 of the SMC proper-motion study lies at RA 01 15 34.1, Dec -72 50 49.3, matching this pointing (RA 18.892, Dec -72.847)
The fields were chosen to contain background quasars
The study measured the proper motion (motion across the sky) of the SMC
The outer SMC shows ordered motion away from the galaxy, indicating tidal disruption
The work is tied to HST program GO-13476
